subject.title: fix(qwen): correct Token Plan catalog limits and input modalities

question: Should OpenClaw continue using one shared Token Plan catalog for China and Global when this correction is only proven against Global/Singapore, or should the catalog become endpoint-specific before these values change?
rationale: The contributor has established a real Global contract but cannot currently test China, and the existing shared-catalog structure makes either decision affect China users as well.

options.title: Hold for China proof
options.body: Keep the shared catalog and merge only after redacted China accept/reject and video-content evidence confirms every changed value.

options.title: Split regional catalog metadata
options.body: Add an endpoint-scoped catalog path so Global corrections can land without asserting the same limits and modalities for China.

options.title: Narrow the PR
options.body: Remove the unverified changes and retain only documentation or values that maintainers can independently establish as shared contracts.

recommendation.title: Hold for China proof
recommendation.body: Keep the shared catalog and merge only after redacted China accept/reject and video-content evidence confirms every changed value.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the live gateway evidence and can clarify or extend the regional validation, while a repository owner must ultimately select the permanent catalog policy.
